title: A stripped master-detail repoint unlocks a parent-scoped readonlyWhen: a by-id update judges the lock against the parent it names, not the parent it stores
body:
**Class:** a (pre-existing on `main`; found by the #18682 round-14 dev while fixing the same shape on the traversal seam, and not in PR #19728's diff).

## What happens

A by-id `update()` resolves the `parent` header that `readonlyWhen` judges from the PRE-strip patch, payload FK first:

- `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:12673` on `origin/main` `afc3b64928`: `await this.resolveMasterDetailParent(updateSchema, preRoWhen, priorRecord)`.

When the master-detail FK is declared static `readonly: true`, the strip that removes it runs AFTER the `readonlyWhen` strip has already judged against the parent the caller NAMED. The row keeps its stored parent, but the lock was judged against a different one.

## Measured (the round-14 dev, real engine at `ada09f0953`, memory driver)

- `inv_line.amount` has `readonlyWhen: "parent.status == 'paid'"`; `inv_line.invoice` is `master_detail` with `readonly: true`. Line `l1` sits under paid invoice `inv_a`; `inv_b` is open.
- `update(l1, { amount: 999, invoice: 'inv_b' })` → **committed**, stored `{ amount: 999, invoice: 'inv_a' }`. The paid-invoice lock was bypassed.
- Control: `update(l1, { amount: 555 })` alone → `amount` dropped by the lock (it stayed 999).
- Without `readonly` on `invoice` the repoint lands, and the result is correct.

The seat has read the cited line on `main`; the run itself is the dev's.

## Property wanted

A by-id update judges `readonlyWhen` against the parent the write STORES, i.e. after every strip that can change the FK. PR #19728 fixed the same order on its own seam by resolving from the post-strip merged view (`{ ...priorRecord, ...post-strip data }`); that is a reference, not a prescription.

Dedupe words: readonlyWhen parent repoint strip; resolveMasterDetailParent preRoWhen; master_detail readonly repoint lock bypass; payload-FK-first static readonly.
